title: Petra and the Ledger Again
premise: Oscar Thackeray, the cathedral archivist who catalogues other people's griefs, finds a missing woman's diary in the locked crypt—entries continuing three weeks past her disappearance. As Oscar investigates, she realizes the killer is feeding her clues deliberately, someone who knows the old case files intimately and wants an audience. The trail leads to the cathedral's own found family of vergers, volunteers, and misfits Oscar has come to love, forcing her to choose between protecting them and exposing the truth. In the end Oscar stages a false ledger entry to lure the killer into the crypt, where he confesses that he kept writing the diary himself—to keep his victim 'alive'—and she must decide whether memory can be both a wound and a witness.
about_author: Felix Pemberton spent a decade cataloguing parish records in northern England before turning to crime fiction, a career that left him with an archivist's patience and a coroner's curiosity. He writes in the margins of ledgers and claims every mystery begins with a filing error.

chapters.title: The Locked Crypt
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. During a routine inventory of the sealed crypt, Oscar discovers a leather diary wedged behind a memorial slab—belonging to Marion Voss, missing for three years. The emotional beat is quiet unease: the crypt has been locked since before Marion vanished.

chapters.title: Entries After the End
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Reading by lamplight, she realizes the diary continues twenty-three days past Marion's disappearance date, in handwriting that falters but persists. She reports it to the police and is dismissed. Beat: dread mixed with the thrill of being noticed at last.

chapters.title: The Case File Nobody Read
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Pulling the original investigation file from diocesan archives, she finds pages annotated in fresh pencil—corrections no investigator would make. Someone has studied this case like scripture. Beat: the hunter realizes she is being hunted gently.

chapters.title: Vergers and Volunteers
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Oscar and young verger Tobias. We meet the cathedral's found family: deaf bell-ringer Agnes, ex-con gardener Cyril, skeptical dean. Beat: warmth established—the people Oscar will later have to risk.

chapters.title: What Marion Kept
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The diary reveals Marion was researching the cathedral's restoration fund, tracing discrepancies. Entries grow paranoid about 'the one who counts.' Beat: Oscar recognizes her own loneliness in Marion's voice.

chapters.title: A Note in Her Own Hand
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. A note appears inside the ledger, addressed to Oscar by name, quoting her private marginalia. The killer knows her habits better than her colleagues do. Beat: violation—the invisible woman seen too clearly.

chapters.title: Detective Inspector Reyes
chapters.summary: Reyes' POV. The reopened case brings DI Reyes, sharp and skeptical of the amateur archivist. Their friction masks mutual recognition: two people who hide inside their work. Beat: reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: The Counting House
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Following Marion's financial trail, Oscar finds the restoration fund skimmed for years—a pattern only someone with archive access could sustain. Beat: suspicion turns inward toward the family she loves.

chapters.title: Cyril's Silence
chapters.summary: Tobias' POV. Cyril the gardener is caught burning papers and refuses to explain. The community fractures under whispered accusation. Beat: fear corroding found family.

chapters.title: The Second Diary
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. A second diary surfaces—Marion's earlier volume—in which she names her confidant only as 'A.' Oscar realizes there were two readers of Marion's secret. Beat: the mystery doubles.

chapters.title: Agnes Remembers
chapters.summary: Agnes' POV. The deaf bell-ringer recalls seeing Marion alive after her official disappearance date, meeting a man in the crypt stairwell. Memory, unreliable and precious, becomes evidence. Beat: hope rekindled.

chapters.title: Trap Laid by Another Hand
chapters.summary: Reyes' POV. Reyes sets surveillance on the crypt; the killer anticipates it, leaving a mocking entry dated tomorrow. He knows the investigation's playbook because he once helped write procedure. Beat: the investigators realize the killer may be one of them—or beside them.

chapters.title: The Archivist Before
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Digging into personnel records, Oscar finds a former assistant archivist, Ambrose Pell, dismissed years ago over fund irregularities—who volunteered back weekly. Beat: the shape of the enemy emerges.

chapters.title: Confession in the Bell Tower
chapters.summary: Tobias' POV. Cyril confesses to Tobias that he burned papers to protect Agnes, whom Pell had been blackmailing. Not murder—but complicity of silence. Beat: guilt without villainy; love against duty.

chapters.title: Marion's Last Entry
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The diary's final post-disappearance entry decodes: Marion discovered Pell's thefts, and the continuing entries were written by Pell after her death—keeping her handwriting alive as trophy and alibi. Beat: horror crystallizes.

chapters.title: The Dean's Bargain
chapters.summary: Dean's POV. The dean, fearing scandal, pressures Oscar to hand everything over quietly. Oscar refuses, choosing truth over the institution that gave her shelter. Beat: duty inverted—her real duty is to the dead.

chapters.title: Vanishing Act
chapters.summary: Reyes' POV. Pell stops coming to the cathedral; his flat is scrubbed clean except for a shelf of perfectly ordered case files—including one begun on Oscar herself. Beat: cold terror; she is his next chapter.

chapters.title: The False Ledger
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar proposes the trap: plant a forged ledger entry suggesting the restoration fund's master record—Pell's true insurance—is hidden in the crypt. Beat: resolve; the invisible woman makes herself bait.

chapters.title: Nightwatch
chapters.summary: Alternating Oscar/Reyes POV. The vigil in the dark cathedral; small human moments—Agnes's bells, Tobias's fear, Reyes's steadying hand. Beat: tenderness before violence.

chapters.title: Into the Crypt
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Pell comes, and in the crypt confronts Oscar, confessing he killed Marion when she wouldn't join him, then wrote her life onward because erasing her felt like losing her. Beat: the killer revealed as a warped archivist of love.

chapters.title: Ledger Closed
chapters.summary: Reyes' POV. The arrest; Pell's meticulous files convict him. Marion is formally declared dead, her name read aloud in the cathedral. Beat: justice as remembrance.

chapters.title: What We Keep
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Months later, Oscar places Marion's diaries in a new public archive, open to all, and lets the found family gather around her. Final beat: memory shared is memory survived; Oscar is visible at last, and glad.
